lesson_title: A Nail That Grabs and Lets Go
hook_text: Wind wire round a nail, press a switch, and paper clips leap up. Let go, and they fall. A magnet with an off button.
clip_script: Put a compass next to a wire and send current through. The needle swings. Current makes magnetism. Coil the wire and the little fields stack up into a bar magnet you can switch on and off. Flip the cell and north becomes south. Now slide an iron nail into the coil. Suddenly it lifts a whole chain of clips, because the nail's insides line up with the field and multiply it hundreds of times. Want it stronger? More turns. More current. Always an iron core, never copper. Want it off? Open the switch and the clips drop, because soft iron forgets at once. That is why the scrap crane wants an electromagnet and not a permanent one: it lifts the steel, swings, and lets go on command.
visual_style: Whiteboard wire with a compass twitching; wire wrapping into a coil; nail sliding in and clips leaping; switch opening and clips falling.
mood: Delighted and demonstrative, one surprise after another.
pacing: Twitch, coil, flip, nail, grab, drop, each beat a second or two.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and wind your own electromagnet on a nail.
